finding: §2.2's load-bearing paragraph asserts an architecture the twin it copies does not have. It says: 'ReviewRound.Clean is stamped at record time, so a round recorded in 2026 is never re-graded under a knob set later: those 67 rows are read by no predicate this release adds.' That is true of TODAY's audit path (audit_record.go:71 stamps clean := findings == 0 and engine.Converged -> ConsecutiveClean reads the stamped flag), but §2 says four times that this release is the twin of review_converge_on, and the twin does the opposite: ReviewConsecutiveClean (engine/reviewclean.go:119-128) re-grades EVERY recorded round live via ReviewRoundClean(specPath, &rounds[i], convergeOn), and engine/reviewclean.go:91-93 states the choice as a design intent -- 'Read live from the round's recorded findings ... so a later --resolve or converge-on switch re-evaluates it without re-recording'. If the audit side is built as the twin, the 67 legacy rows in 15 files ARE read by the predicate this release adds, §2's fail-closed rule makes all 15 historical round files blocking, and every converged pre-v0.33.0 cycle flips to not-converged on install -- the exact retroactivity §3 cut the release's second deliverable for. §2.2's numbers all verify (67 = high 16 / medium 15 / low 36 across 15 files; 238 non-PASS and 0 out-of-enum across v0.33.0-v0.36.0; 2,913 PASS rows all severity null); only its premise does not.
suggestion: §2 must state whether audit_converge_on is evaluated at record time or live per round, and §2.2 must then be rewritten to whichever it is. If record-time: say so explicitly and say that this DIVERGES from review_converge_on, and drop 'this is its twin'. If live: §2.2's dismissal of the 67 rows is false and the retroactive-blocking outcome needs the same decision §3 deferred to spec/0.46.0.md §8.4.

finding: §2's repaired sentence 'the enum's cardinality is asserted in nine places that must move with it, counted' is miscounted in both directions, measured against the tree. Of the nine listed, engine/escalation.go:29 asserts NO cardinality -- it reads '// escalationDecisions is the closed set in the order §5.2 writes it, which is' and names no number. The 'not a sixth category' comment §2 quotes as being among 14,29,39,47 is at :19-20, not :29. Three sites that DO assert the cardinality are missing from the list: engine/escalation.go:19 ('not a sixth category'), internal/cli/escalate_test.go:154 ('pins §5.2's closed set') and internal/cli/escalate_test.go:157 -- the function NAME TestEscalateAcceptsTheFiveDecisions. A repo-wide scan for /[Ff]ive|sixth/ within four lines of decision|escalat|skip-gate|import-force returns eleven such sites, not nine (the eight correct listed ones plus those three; escalate_test.go:72's 'five variables' is about env vars and is correctly excluded). Worse for testability: none of the eleven goes red on a sixth entry. TestEscalateAcceptsTheFiveDecisions loops the five string literals and asserts each is ACCEPTED (escalate_test.go:158-168), so it passes unchanged once a sixth exists, leaving a test function whose name says five while the enum holds six. §5 test 10 pins only that a refusal names audit-converge-on, so nothing in the release's acceptance detects the drift.
suggestion: Re-derive the list against the tree (drop :29, add :19, :154 and :157, say eleven), or -- better, per this repo's own rule that a claim a guard enforces cannot drift -- replace the prose count with a guard: assert len(engine.EscalationDecisions()) == 6 in engine/escalation_test.go and add that assertion to §5 test 10, so a seventh entry cannot land without the count moving.

finding: §4's closing paragraph delegates the SECOND deliberately reversed guard to a test that does not contain it. It says of internal/cli/docs_contract_test.go:96 -- which pins the literal 'audit convergence still counts every non-PASS row' in SKILL.md -- 'This release updates both, and §5 test 3's doc assertions are over that sentence and SKILL.md:145's --status --check clause'. §5 test 3 has no doc assertion: it reads in full 'The two surfaces v0.31.1 exists for. tp config --extract emits the field and tp validate --project accepts and rejects it'. So the release names two sentences it falsifies, names the shipped guard that reddens, and then routes the acceptance to a test about a different subject. The consequence is the hazard §4 itself raises one paragraph earlier for the FIRST guard: an implementer with spec cover for 'reversing the guard' can satisfy the suite by DELETING docs_contract_test.go:96 rather than updating its literal, and no test in §5 distinguishes the two outcomes. §4 protects the first guard by naming three of its nine surviving assertions; the second guard gets no such protection.
suggestion: Either add a §5 test 12 pinning the two replacement literals (the new SKILL.md sentence and the new SKILL.md:145 --status --check clause) and asserting docs_contract_test.go still contains a doc-contract assertion over each, or extend test 3 to actually carry them and say so in its text. Do not leave §4 pointing at test 3 for assertions test 3 does not make.

finding: Re-check of test 8's !StateStale barrier, requested for this round. The barrier is REAL but CONDITIONAL, and the current wording does not choose the condition. Facts: engine.Converged = ConsecutiveClean(rounds) >= n && !StateStale(rounds, currentHash) (engine/reviewstate.go:509-511); audit --record (audit_record.go:95) and --status/--check (audit_record.go:333, exit at :401) both go through it with the LIVE hash of the spec argument; and clean is stamped once at record time (audit_record.go:71, clean := findings == 0), so nothing on the audit path ever re-grades a stored round. Two constructions satisfy test 8's words and give different answers. (1) Replay by RE-RECORDING: write each round's copied rows to a file and run `tp audit <fixture-spec> --record` nine and thirteen times. Each record stamps spec_hash from the fixture spec, StateStale is false, and the pinned answers are reachable -- I confirmed the arithmetic against the corpus: blocking 3 / all 9 for v0.35.0 and blocking 3 / all never for v0.36.0 at audit_clean_rounds 2, and 2 and 8 at 1, exactly as §2.1 and test 8 state. (2) Replay by SYNTHESISING round entries -- load the rows, compute clean per policy, build []ReviewRound, call Converged prefix-wise -- where StateStale compares the last synthesised entry's SpecHash against whatever hash the test passes; unless the author deliberately makes them equal, Converged is false for every prefix and 3 and 9 are unreachable, and the natural 'fix' is to assert ConsecutiveClean instead, which silently drops the staleness half of convergence out of the test's coverage. Test 8 says only 'the rows ... copied into testdata/ ... reproduce §2.1's table' and names no fixture spec, no command, and no function. Worse, the two constructions are not free choices: (1) is only available if audit_converge_on is evaluated at RECORD time and (2) only if it is evaluated LIVE, and that is the decision §2 has not made (§2.2's paragraph appears to make it and is refuted by the twin -- see my §2.2 row). Verdict: as written, test 8 does not reach its numbers; it reaches them under one of two constructions the release has not chosen between.
suggestion: Pin the construction. State the command form and the fixture: e.g. 'a temp-dir fixture spec whose bytes do not change across the replay, the rows of each recorded round fed to `tp audit spec.md --record round-N.ndjson` in order, asserting the round at which the emitted converged first becomes true'. Then state that spec_hash is stamped per record so stale stays false, and add the negative arm -- touching the fixture spec after the last record makes converged false -- so the staleness half is covered rather than accidentally excluded. This is unwritable until §2 states record-time vs live evaluation.

finding: Test 10 asserts an observable tp does not produce, and tests 9 and 10 together leave the refusal's only real observable unpinned. Test 10 reads 'A fenced refusal RECORDS --decision audit-converge-on, not other'. A fenced refusal records nothing: refuseUnattended (internal/cli/unattended.go:33-38) and refuseUnattendedCommandField (:44-49) print an output.Error whose HINT is the string 'escalate instead: tp escalate --decision <name> --evidence <what you found>' and exit 2. The only writer of an escalation record is `tp escalate` itself (engine/escalation.go, cli/escalate.go), which the unit runs afterwards. So one engineer asserts the refusal's hint text contains audit-converge-on (passes against a correct implementation) and another asserts a $TP_RUN_DIR/$TP_UNIT_SEQ-escalation.json appears carrying decision: audit-converge-on (fails against every correct implementation). Second half: §2's own code sketch tells the implementer to copy the guard `if engine.Unattended() && engine.FencedCommandField(field) { refuseUnattendedCommandField(field)` at set.go:361-362 and set_project.go:46-47. An implementer who reuses refuseUnattendedCommandField for the third predicate ships the message 'audit_converge_on names a command the driver executes and cannot be set under TP_UNATTENDED, at any layer' -- false, the field names no command -- and BOTH test 9 (exit 2 on each path) and test 10 (the decision name in the hint) still pass, because neither pins the message. §2's whole argument for the enum entry is that 'the reason [is] recoverable only from free text', i.e. it is about message quality, and no test in §5 asserts any of it.
suggestion: Rewrite test 10 as 'a fenced refusal exits 2 and its hint names `tp escalate --decision audit-converge-on`, not `other`' -- the observable tp actually emits -- and add to test 9 an assertion on the refusal MESSAGE, pinning that it names audit_converge_on as a convergence policy and not as a command the driver executes, so reusing refuseUnattendedCommandField goes red.

finding: §1's repair left a sentence that narrates §1's own past state inside the paragraph an implementer derives scope from: 'This paragraph described the two-deliverable release for one round after the cut, which is the shape of defect §3 exists to stop the next reader re-proposing.' Nothing in it is testable and nothing in it is a requirement -- it is a claim about the file's revision history, made three lines after §3 is already cited for the cut and in a release whose own header quotes spec/0.43.0.md §2's repair-verbosity class as the reason 77 lines of withdrawal prose were deleted. It also introduces a small ambiguity of tense a scanning reader can invert: the paragraph opens 'One deliverable' and closes by saying the paragraph described two.
suggestion: Delete the sentence. §3 already records the cut and why re-proposing it is the defect; §1's job is to say what ships.
